requirements.protection: Least privilege, MFA, revocation within four hours of role change/termination, quarterly access review and cited AC/Category 2 alignment.
requirements.limitation: MFA and stale-account detection do not establish least privilege or four-hour revocation; expert sampling and role definitions limit assurance.
requirements.evidence_needed: Compare actual privilege and role-change records, timed deprovisioning, session/token invalidation and quarterly remediation.
requirements.potential_harm: Stale or excessive privilege enables unauthorized issuance or key use.
requirements.disposition_rationale: Privilege and deprovisioning bounds are prescribed; actual role-change and session-invalidation evidence is needed to establish timely withdrawal.

requirements.protection: Access-level-commensurate screening, annual training, separation of duties and cited PS/Category 4 alignment.
requirements.limitation: Personnel records do not verify behavior; expert sampling is incomplete.
requirements.evidence_needed: Review role-specific screening criteria, training and actual separation in critical operations without collecting personnel data.
requirements.potential_harm: Personnel misuse or unchecked critical actions compromise issuance.
requirements.disposition_rationale: Screening, training and separation are stated; role-specific evidence is necessary to establish their operation without collecting unnecessary personnel data.

requirements.protection: Quarterly scans of all components, annual independent penetration tests, severity-based patch timelines and cited RA/SI/Category 8 alignment.
requirements.limitation: Scan coverage gaps, engagement scope and test duration limit conclusions.
requirements.evidence_needed: Reconcile actual component inventory, scan scope, independent tester qualifications, patch deadlines and remediation evidence; no operational penetration testing performed.
requirements.disposition_rationale: Scan and remediation intervals are prescribed; inventory, coverage and remediation evidence are necessary to establish that the actual system is included.

requirements.protection: Security-event logging, minimum retention, cryptographic integrity, continuous monitoring and explicit exclusion of holder-identifying presentation information; cited AU/Categories 6–7 alignment.
requirements.limitation: AUTO cannot establish all-subsystem instrumentation; EXPT sampling bounded. ADMN N/A limitation nevertheless describes organizational policy/retention review.
requirements.evidence_needed: Inspect actual log scope, integrity and retention, negative privacy checks across all subsystems and monitoring evidence; clarify method assignment.
requirements.potential_harm: Audit blind spots or presentation surveillance undermine accountability/privacy.
requirements.disposition_rationale: The verification-method assignment needs clarification for expert and administrative review of monitoring and privacy exclusions; actual log evidence remains necessary.

source.member: SEDI RAHP Review Input/SEDI Implementation Guide/Part 9_ Cross-Cutting Technical Requirements _ SEDI.pdf

requirements.protection: Documented response/recovery, automated alerting, defined initiation timeline, lawful breach notification, corrective-action closure, annual review/exercise and cited IR/Category 8 alignment.
requirements.limitation: Documentation and exercises do not establish real-incident effectiveness; automated alerting addressed in ORG-04.
requirements.evidence_needed: Inspect alert-to-response timing, exercise and actual incident records where available, notification basis and corrective-action verification.
requirements.potential_harm: Delayed containment or recovery causes cascading harm or service interruption.
requirements.disposition_rationale: Response and recovery duties are defined; exercise and incident records are required to establish timing, notification and verified closure.

requirements.protection: Delegated third parties subject to all applicable KMS/ORG obligations, equivalent written agreements, annual independent audit, function inventory and retained Department accountability; cited SA alignment.
requirements.limitation: Audit scope/frequency bounded by contract; contract review does not establish operational behavior.
requirements.evidence_needed: Map delegated functions to obligations and inventory, inspect actual operational custody, subdelegation, audit coverage and remediation; reconcile with state control and sole Department HSM operational control.
requirements.potential_harm: Delegation creates unaccountable infrastructure or key custody gaps.
requirements.disposition_rationale: The interaction between delegated operation, state custody and sole Department HSM control needs clarification before delegated functions can be assessed against the intended authority boundary.

requirements.protection: Significant changes require risk assessment, production-mirroring tests, authorized approval and rollback; emergency expedited review/reconciliation; cited CM/Category 1 alignment.
requirements.limitation: Records do not establish quality; expert sampling misses changes.
requirements.evidence_needed: Inspect change classification, test fidelity, approvals, rollback and emergency reconciliation; examine evidence invalidation and targeted reassessment.
requirements.potential_harm: Material changes invalidate prior assurance while stale claims remain in use.
requirements.disposition_rationale: Change-control and rollback requirements are explicit; actual approvals, test fidelity and reassessment evidence are needed to establish that material changes do not bypass them.

cases.constructed: Delegated operator's role ends, but a previously authorized privileged session or credential remains usable beyond the four-hour revocation boundary.
cases.evidence: Check role-change time, all applicable access paths, active session/token invalidation, third-party responsibility and actual Department oversight; distinguish account disablement from loss of effective privilege.

cases.constructed: Security logs have integrity and alerting but include linkable holder presentation identifiers, or omit a critical subsystem.
cases.evidence: Inspect actual coverage and log content across subsystems; exercise critical alert and incident response without introducing presentation tracking. Clarify ADMN N/A versus policy review limitation.

cases.constructed: Emergency patch changes a material control; previously successful conformance evidence is retained without assessing its applicability to the changed configuration.
cases.evidence: Inspect scope, authorized expedited review, post-change reconciliation, rollback and affected evidence; test whether stale evidence remains distinguishable from current evidence.

limitations: ORG denotes organizational security, not organizational identity. Part 9 p44 defines the domain and applicability to the Department and delegated infrastructure operators via ORG-06.
ORG-04 ADMN N/A limitation describes organizational policy review; preserve source method applicability and seek clarification.
ORG-06 lists delegated key custody and hosting as examples; their relationship to SDI-13/KMS-03 state/sole Department control needs explicit interpretation, not presumed permission.
Part 9 pp60–62 is informative technology limitations; use it to qualify control claims, not invent numbered requirements.
No implementation evidence, independent review, risk scoring, guardrail verification or legal determination.
